3.title: Numbers and contact details
objectives: recognise the digits from zero to nine
give a fictional phone number
ask for information to be repeated

production.writingPrompt: Fill in a fictional form with a name, town and number. Then write a request to repeat the information.
production.speakingPrompt: Dictate a made-up number digit by digit, then ask your partner to repeat their number.
criteria: Use fictional details only.
Say the digits clearly.
Include “Kan du gjenta?”.

conversationPrompts: Kan du si tallene fra null til fem?
Can you say the numbers from zero to five?
Hva er et oppdiktet telefonnummer?
What is a made-up phone number?
Hvordan ber du noen gjenta nummeret?
How do you ask someone to repeat the number?
vocabulary: Nummeret begynner med null, en, to.
The number starts with zero, one, two.
Jeg sier seks, sju, åtte, ni.
I say six, seven, eight, nine.
dialogue: Anna
Jeg bor i Oslo. Her er nummeret mitt.
I live in Oslo. Here is my number.
Ola
Litt saktere, takk. Hva er nummeret ditt?
A little more slowly, please. What is your number?
Anna
Hva er telefonnummeret ditt?
What is your phone number?
Ola
I øvelsen er det en, to, tre, fire, fem, seks, sju, åtte.
In the exercise, it is one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight.
Anna
Kan du gjenta?
Can you repeat that?
Ola
Ja: en, to, tre, fire, fem, seks, sju, åtte.
Yes: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight.
Anna
Takk. Her er e-postadressen min.
Thank you. Here is my email address.
Ola
Takk! Jeg skriver nummeret.
Thank you! I am writing down the number.

grammar.title: “Hva er ...?” and “Kan du ...?” as set expressions
grammar.rule: “Hva er …?” asks for information. For now, learn “telefonnummeret ditt” as a complete phrase: “your phone number”. “Kan du gjenta?” means “Can you repeat that?”. After “kan”, use “gjenta” without “å”; you can add what needs to be repeated.
examples: Hva er telefonnummeret ditt? — What is your phone number?
Hva er nummeret ditt? — What is your number?
Kan du gjenta? — Can you repeat that?
Kan du gjenta nummeret? — Can you repeat the number?

5.title: Family and people
objectives: talk about your family
use simple definite forms
express possession with “min” and “din”

production.writingPrompt: Introduce a made-up family in three statements: two people and where they live.
production.speakingPrompt: Talk about a fictional family member: their name, where they live and one quality.
criteria: Use a family word.
Include “min” or “mine” after the appropriate form.
Give the name and place of residence.

conversationPrompts: Har du søsken?
Do you have any brothers or sisters?
Hvor bor familien din?
Where does your family live?
Hva heter en person i familien din?
What is the name of someone in your family?
dialogue: Anna
Jeg heter Anna. Broren min heter Dan.
My name is Anna. My brother is called Dan.
Dan
Jeg bor i Oslo med familien min.
I live in Oslo with my family.
Erik
Har du en bror eller en søster?
Do you have a brother or a sister?
Ana
Ja, jeg har en bror.
Yes, I have a brother.
Erik
Hvor bor broren din?
Where does your brother live?
Ana
Broren min bor i Oslo.
My brother lives in Oslo.
Erik
Hva heter broren din?
What is your brother's name?

grammar.title: The verb in second position
grammar.rule: In a declarative main clause, the finite verb is the second element. “I dag” is one unit of meaning, even though it has two words: “I dag | jobber | jeg”. For the day of the week here, use “på mandag”. For the meeting time, use “klokka” followed by the number: “klokka ni”.

objectives: name free-time activities

dialogue: Anna
I dag har jeg fri. Jeg går en tur.

grammar.title: Frequency and verb position

Noen ganger leser jeg hjemme. — Sometimes I read at home.

Jeg hører på musikk hver dag. — I listen to music every day.

13.title: At the café
objectives: place a simple order
use polite expressions
recognise the Bokmål articles “en” and “et”

production.writingPrompt: Write an order with a drink, something to eat and a polite expression.
production.speakingPrompt: Order at a café and politely accept or decline an offer.
criteria: Use “Jeg vil ha”.
Keep the item's article, “en” or “et”.
Include “takk”.

conversationPrompts: Hva vil du bestille?
What would you like to order?
Vil du ha et smørbrød?
Would you like a sandwich?
Vil du ha kaffe eller vann?
Would you like coffee or water?
dialogue: Anna
Vi møtes på kafé i dag.
We are meeting at the café today.
Lars
Først vil jeg gå en tur. Etterpå vil jeg ha en kaffe.
First I want to go for a walk. Afterwards I want a coffee.
Client
Hei! Jeg vil ha en kaffe, takk.
Hello! I would like a coffee, please.
Servitør
Vil du ha et smørbrød?
Would you like a sandwich?
Client
Ja, takk.
Yes, please.
Servitør
En kaffe og et smørbrød.
A coffee and a sandwich.
Client
Kan jeg få vann også?

Ja, her er vannet.

grammar.title: The Bokmål articles “en” and “et”
grammar.rule: Learn each singular noun with its article: “en kaffe”, “et smørbrød”. In these Bokmål examples, the article goes before the noun; not every noun uses “en”. For a simple order, use “Jeg vil ha” followed by the item. “Vil” is followed by “ha”, without “å”; you can add “takk” to be polite.
examples: en kaffe — a coffee
et smørbrød — a sandwich
Jeg vil ha vann. — I would like some water.
Jeg vil ha en kaffe. — I would like a coffee.

grammar.title: Questions with “hva” and “hvor”

15.title: Shopping lists and preferences
objectives: make a short list

production.writingPrompt: Write a list of three items to buy with two quantities and one sentence about preferences.
production.speakingPrompt: Ask for bread, milk and apples; specify the quantity for two products.
criteria: Include two units or numbers.

conversationPrompts: Hva trenger du til frokost?

Liker du epler?

Vil du ha to epler eller et kilo?

Jeg vil ha et kilo epler.

dialogue: Anna
Hvor mye? Jeg trenger også to epler.

Ansatt
Har du et kort? Du kan betale her.

Anna

Trenger vi epler også?

grammar.title: Quantity and the plural “epler”
grammar.rule: In this lesson, “et eple” becomes “to epler” after a number greater than one. Do not keep the singular article “et” before the plural. “Et kilo epler” specifies the quantity. Revisit “ikke” after the verb, now for preferences: “jeg liker ikke”. Keep the same order when saying which foods you dislike.

Jeg vil ha et kilo epler. — I would like a kilogram of apples.
Jeg liker ikke melk. — I do not like milk.
Jeg liker ikke epler. — I do not like apples.

grammar.title: Location with “i”, destination with “til”

conversationPrompts: Hvor går bussen?

vocabulary: The bus goes to the town centre.

dialogue: Anna
Sentrum er målet. Hvilken buss tar jeg?

grammar.title: The imperative for instructions
grammar.rule: Use the imperative for a direct instruction: “gå”, “ta”, “vent”. The imperative of “å gå” is “gå”; for “å vente”, it is “vent”, so it is not just a matter of removing “å”. Reuse the request “Jeg vil ha”, now with “en billett”. Add “til Oslo” to specify where you want to go.

19.title: Weather and clothing
objectives: describe the weather
say what clothes you need
use the construction “det er”

production.writingPrompt: Write three statements: today's weather, what clothing you need and how you are getting to the town centre.
production.speakingPrompt: Describe the weather and choose between walking and taking the bus.
criteria: Use “Det er” or “Det regner”.
Name an item of clothing or a useful object.
Link the weather to your travel plan.

conversationPrompts: Hvordan er været i dag?
What is the weather like today?
Hva trenger du når det regner?
What do you need when it rains?
Er det kaldt eller varmt ute?
Is it cold or warm outside?
vocabulary: What is the weather like today?
dialogue: Anna
Jeg vil gå en tur, men det regner.
I want to go for a walk, but it is raining.
Lars
En buss går til sentrum. Ta en jakke.
A bus goes to the town centre. Take a jacket.
Mia
Hvordan er været i dag?
What is the weather like today?
Dan
Det er kaldt og det regner.
It is cold and raining.
Mia
Jeg trenger en varm jakke.
I need a warm jacket.
Dan
Ja, og jeg har en paraply.
Yes, and I have an umbrella.
Mia
Går vi en tur i dag?
Shall we go for a walk today?
Dan
Ja, men vi trenger en paraply.
Yes, but we need an umbrella.

grammar.title: The construction “det er”
grammar.rule: For the weather descriptions in this lesson, use “det er” plus an adjective: “kaldt”, “varmt”. Keep “det”, just as English uses “it” in “it is cold”. “Jeg trenger” means “I need”. The thing you need follows the verb directly: “jeg trenger en jakke”, with no preposition.
examples: Det er kaldt ute. — It is cold outside.
Det er varmt inne. — It is warm inside.
Jeg trenger en varm jakke. — I need a warm jacket.
Jeg trenger en paraply. — I need an umbrella.
grammar.wrong: Det kaldt er ute.

objectives: introduce yourself to a colleague

production.writingPrompt: Write a three-sentence message to a colleague: an introduction, a question about the meeting and a request for help.
production.speakingPrompt: Introduce yourself to a colleague, ask the meeting time and ask them to send an email.
criteria: Include an introduction.

conversationPrompts: Hva heter kollegaen i dialogen?

vocabulary: The meeting is at ten o'clock.
dialogue: Anna
I dag er jeg på jobb.

Erik
Jeg trenger en kollega til møtet. Vil du bli med?

22.title: Understanding, asking and confirming
objectives: say when you do not understand
ask for an explanation or demonstration
confirm a simple instruction

production.writingPrompt: Write four lines between a colleague and someone asking for a demonstration and checking the result.
production.speakingPrompt: Ask for an instruction to be repeated, ask for a demonstration and confirm that you have finished.
criteria: Use two different requests for help.
Include “Er dette riktig?”.
Finish with a short confirmation.

conversationPrompts: Hva sier du når du ikke forstår?
What do you say when you do not understand?
Hvordan ber du noen snakke saktere?
How do you ask someone to speak more slowly?
Hvordan spør du om noe er riktig?
How do you ask whether something is correct?
vocabulary: I do not understand the task.
Can you show me the table?
Si det en gang til, takk.
I have finished with the table.
dialogue: Anna
Kan du gjenta? Jeg forstår ikke.
Can you repeat that? I do not understand.
Erik
Ja, jeg kan hjelpe deg. Se her.
Yes, I can help you. Look here.
Erik
Sett koppen på bordet, takk.
Put the cup on the table, please.
Anna
Jeg forstår ikke. Kan du vise meg?
I do not understand. Can you show me?
Erik
Ja. Koppen skal stå her.
Yes. The cup should go here.
Anna
Her? Er dette riktig?
Here? Is this correct?
Erik
Ja, det er riktig.
Yes, that is correct.
Anna
Takk. Nå er jeg ferdig.
Thank you. Now I have finished.

Kan du snakke saktere? — Can you speak more slowly?
Er dette riktig? — Is this correct?
Dette er riktig. — This is correct.

23.title: A break and a simple invitation
objectives: invite a colleague for a break
accept or decline politely
suggest a simple alternative

production.writingPrompt: Write a four-line exchange: an invitation for a break, a polite refusal, another time and acceptance.
production.speakingPrompt: Invite a colleague for coffee and find a suitable time if they cannot come now.
criteria: Include an invitation and a reply.
Decline politely with “dessverre”.
Agree on a specific time.

conversationPrompts: Vil du bli med på en pause?
Would you like to join us for a break?
Hvordan sier du nei på en høflig måte?
How do you say no politely?
Når passer det å ta en kaffe?
When is a good time to have a coffee?
vocabulary: Vi tar en pause klokka ti.
We take a break at ten o'clock.
Vi går på kafé. Vil du bli med?
We are going to the café. Would you like to come?
Takk for i dag. God helg!
Thank you for today. Have a good weekend!
dialogue: Anna
En kaffe etter møtet? Passer det?
A coffee after the meeting? Does that suit you?
Erik
Ja, det passer. Vi tar en pause.
Yes, that suits me. We will take a break.
Anna
Vi tar en pause. Vil du bli med?
We are taking a break. Would you like to come?
Erik
Dessverre kan jeg ikke nå.
Unfortunately, I cannot right now.
Anna
Kanskje senere? Passer klokka to?
Maybe later? Does two o'clock suit you?
Erik
Ja, gjerne. Vi møtes klokka to.
Yes, gladly. We will meet at two o'clock.
Anna
Da tar vi en kaffe sammen.
Then we will have a coffee together.
Erik
Fint! Og god helg etter jobb!
Good! And have a good weekend after work!

grammar.title: Questions and answers with “kan”
grammar.rule: Decline with “jeg kan ikke”. If you start with “Dessverre”, the finite verb comes before the person: “Dessverre kan jeg ikke”. “Ikke” stays after the person in this example. “Ja, gjerne!” is a complete, polite response to an invitation. You can follow it with a specific suggestion, using the meeting phrases.
examples: Jeg kan ikke nå. — I cannot right now.
Dessverre kan jeg ikke nå. — Unfortunately, I cannot right now.
Ja, gjerne! — Yes, gladly!
Ja, gjerne. Vi møtes klokka to. — Yes, gladly. We will meet at two o'clock.

1.title: Plans and invitations
objectives: invite someone to an activity
accept or decline politely
agree on a day and time

production.writingPrompt: Write a four-sentence invitation with an activity, day, time and meeting place.
production.speakingPrompt: Invite a friend and negotiate the meeting day and time in simple terms.
criteria: Include four practical details.
Distinguish “skal” from “kan”.
Finish by confirming the plan.

conversationPrompts: Hva skal du gjøre på lørdag?
What are you going to do on Saturday?
Har du lyst til å ta en kaffe etter jobb?
Would you like to have a coffee after work?
Når passer det å møtes?
When is a good time for us to meet?
vocabulary: Har du lyst til å ta en kaffe?
Would you like to have a coffee?
Vil du bli med på tur?
Would you like to come for a walk with us?
I am looking forward to it
I am looking forward to Saturday.
dialogue: Anna
Vil du bli med? Vi tar en kaffe etter jobb.
Would you like to come? We are having a coffee after work.
Lars
Passer det på lørdag? Da har jeg bedre tid.
Does Saturday suit you? I have more time then.
Anna
Har du lyst til å ta en kaffe etter jobb?
Would you like to have a coffee after work?
Lars
Ja, gjerne. Når passer det?
Yes, gladly. When is a good time?
Anna
Passer klokka seks?
Does six o'clock suit you?
Lars
Ja, det passer. Jeg gleder meg!
Yes, that suits me. I am looking forward to it!
Anna
Vi skal møtes utenfor kafeen.
We will meet in front of the café.
Lars
Flott, vi ses på lørdag!
Great, see you on Saturday!

grammar.title: Plans with “skal” and suggestions with “kan”
grammar.rule: Here, “skal” introduces an arranged plan, while “kan” introduces a possibility. Both are followed by an infinitive without “å”: “skal møtes”, “kan møtes”. In “Har du lyst til å …?”, keep “til å” before the activity. Compare this with “vil” and “kan”, after which you do not add “å”.
examples: Vi skal møtes på lørdag. — We are going to meet on Saturday.
Vi kan møtes etter jobb. — We can meet after work.
Har du lyst til å ta en kaffe? — Would you like to have a coffee?
Har du lyst til å gå en tur? — Would you like to go for a walk?
grammar.wrong: Vi skal å møtes på lørdag.

points.title: Plans and possibilities
points.explanation: Here, “skal” introduces an arranged plan, while “kan” introduces a possibility. Both are followed by an infinitive without “å”: “skal møtes”, “kan møtes”.

examples.norwegian: Vi kan møtes etter jobb.

contrast.after: Vi skal møtes på lørdag.
contrast.explanation: Here, “skal” introduces an arranged plan, while “kan” introduces a possibility. Both are followed by an infinitive without “å”: “skal møtes”, “kan møtes”.

points.title: Invitations with “lyst til å”
points.explanation: In “Har du lyst til å …?”, keep “til å” before the activity. Compare this with “vil” and “kan”, after which you do not add “å”.

examples.romanian: Would you like to have a coffee?

examples.norwegian: Har du lyst til å gå en tur?

contrast.explanation: The complete phrase in the invitation is “lyst til å”, followed by the verb.

recall.title: Accepting briefly with “gjerne”
recall.explanation: “Ja, gjerne!” is a complete, polite response to an invitation. You can follow it with a specific suggestion, using the meeting phrases.

examples.norwegian: Ja, gjerne!
examples.romanian: Yes, gladly!

examples.norwegian: Ja, gjerne. Vi møtes klokka to.
examples.romanian: Yes, gladly. We will meet at two o'clock.

contrast.before: Dessverre kan jeg ikke nå.
contrast.after: Ja, gjerne!
contrast.explanation: To accept the invitation, use “Ja, gjerne”; the first reply would decline it.

2.title: Meeting people and choosing an activity
objectives: talk about activities together
express a preference between two options
make a suggestion that takes your partner into account

production.writingPrompt: Write a five-sentence message: suggest two activities, choose one and confirm the meeting.
production.speakingPrompt: Choose between a visit and a walk with a friend and explain your preference.
criteria: Present two options.
Use “liker å” and “vil heller”.
Confirm the chosen activity.

conversationPrompts: Hva liker du å gjøre sammen med venner?
What do you like doing with friends?
Vil du heller lese eller gå en tur?
Would you rather read or go for a walk?
Hvordan blir du kjent med nye mennesker?
How do you get to know new people?
vocabulary: Jeg vil bli kjent med naboene.
I want to get to know the neighbours.
Vi besøker en venn på lørdag.
We are visiting a friend on Saturday.
Jeg vil heller gå en tur.
I would rather go for a walk.
Vi har en avtale klokka seks.
We have an appointment at six o'clock.
dialogue: Anna
Har du lyst til å lese på biblioteket?
Would you like to read at the library?
Lars
Jeg liker å lese, men jeg vil heller gå en tur i dag.
I like reading, but today I would rather go for a walk.
Anna
Skal vi besøke Nora på lørdag?
Shall we visit Nora on Saturday?
Lars
Gjerne. Jeg vil bli bedre kjent med henne.
Gladly. I want to get to know her better.
Anna
Vil du lage middag sammen?
Would you like to make dinner together?
Lars
Jeg vil heller gå en tur først.
I would rather go for a walk first.
Anna
Det vil jeg også. Etterpå lager vi middag.
I would like that too. Afterwards we will make dinner.
Lars
Da har vi en avtale!
Then it is a plan!

grammar.title: “Liker å” and “vil heller”
grammar.rule: “Vil heller” chooses one activity over another. After “vil”, the verb has no “å”, even when “heller” comes between them. To say you like an activity, use “liker å” plus the verb. Distinguish this from “vil heller”, which does not keep “å”.
examples: Jeg vil heller gå en tur. — I would rather go for a walk.
Jeg vil heller lese. — I would rather read.
Jeg liker å lese. — I like reading.
Jeg liker å lage middag. — I like making dinner.
grammar.wrong: Jeg vil heller å gå en tur.

points.title: Preferences with “vil heller”
points.explanation: “Vil heller” chooses one activity over another. After “vil”, the verb has no “å”, even when “heller” comes between them.

3.title: Family now and simple changes
objectives: compare ages and homes
distinguish “nå” from “før”
expand a description of someone close to you

production.writingPrompt: Describe an imaginary family in five statements and include two comparisons.
production.speakingPrompt: Introduce someone close to you and compare two rooms in their home.
criteria: Include two comparatives.
Use “enn” to introduce a comparison.
Distinguish “nå” from “før”.

conversationPrompts: Er broren i dialogen yngre eller eldre?
Is the brother in the dialogue younger or older?
Er kjøkkenet større enn før?
Is the kitchen bigger than before?
Hvordan er familien din nå?
What is your family like now?
vocabulary: Broren min er yngre enn meg.
My brother is younger than me.
Søsteren min er eldre enn meg.
My sister is older than me.
Vi bor i et større hus nå.
Now we live in a bigger house.
Dette rommet er mindre enn stuen.
This room is smaller than the living room.
Now the family lives in Oslo.
We used to live in Bergen.
dialogue: Anna
Jeg har en bror. Han er yngre enn meg.
I have a brother. He is younger than me.
Lars
Jeg har en søster. Hun er eldre enn meg.
I have a sister. She is older than me.
Anna
Er broren din eldre enn deg?
Is your brother older than you?
Lars
Nei, han er yngre enn meg.
No, he is younger than me.
Anna
Bor han sammen med familien?
Does he live with the family?
Lars
Ja. Nå bor de i et større hus.
Yes. Now they live in a bigger house.
Anna
Er kjøkkenet større enn før?
Is the kitchen bigger than before?
Lars
Ja, men soverommet er mindre.
Yes, but the bedroom is smaller.

grammar.title: Comparisons with “enn”
grammar.rule: When naming what you are comparing something with, use “enn”: “yngre enn meg”. Some comparatives are irregular: “stor – større”, “liten – mindre”. “Nå” can open a statement to contrast the present with the past. The verb follows, then the person, just as after “I dag”.
examples: Hun er eldre enn meg. — She is older than me.
Dette rommet er mindre enn stuen. — This room is smaller than the living room.
Nå bor de i et større hus. — Now they live in a bigger house.
Nå bor familien i Oslo. — Now the family lives in Oslo.
grammar.wrong: Hun er eldre som meg.

points.title: The comparative and “enn”
points.explanation: When naming what you are comparing something with, use “enn”: “yngre enn meg”. Some comparatives are irregular: “stor – større”, “liten – mindre”.

examples.norwegian: Hun er eldre enn meg.
examples.romanian: She is older than me.

examples.norwegian: Dette rommet er mindre enn stuen.
examples.romanian: This room is smaller than the living room.

contrast.before: Hun er eldre som meg.
contrast.after: Hun er eldre enn meg.
contrast.explanation: When naming what you are comparing something with, use “enn”: “yngre enn meg”. Some comparatives are irregular: “stor – større”, “liten – mindre”.

points.title: Introduce a change with “nå”
points.explanation: “Nå” can open a statement to contrast the present with the past. The verb follows, then the person, just as after “I dag”.

examples.norwegian: Nå bor de i et større hus.
examples.romanian: Now they live in a bigger house.

examples.norwegian: Nå bor familien i Oslo.
examples.romanian: Now the family lives in Oslo.

contrast.before: Nå de bor i et større hus.
contrast.after: Nå bor de i et større hus.
contrast.explanation: After the opening element “Nå”, the verb “bor” precedes the subject “de”.

recall.title: “Min” in the singular, “mine” in the plural
recall.explanation: With the “en” nouns in these examples, the possessive after the noun is “min”: “broren min”. In the plural, use “mine”: “foreldrene mine”. Learn these phrases for now; “min bror” is also correct, with the noun in its indefinite form.

examples.norwegian: Broren min bor i Oslo.
examples.romanian: My brother lives in Oslo.

examples.norwegian: Foreldrene mine bor i Romania.
examples.romanian: My parents live in Romania.

contrast.before: Foreldrene min bor i Romania.
contrast.after: Foreldrene mine bor i Romania.
contrast.explanation: “Foreldrene” is plural, so the possessive is “mine”, not “min”.

4.title: Mission: Plan an activity with a friend and choose a suitable option together.
objectives: Develop an invitation, explain preferences and talk about people close to you.
reuse the section's phrases without checking the translation first
check what you can do on your own and what you need to practise again

production.writingPrompt: Write an exchange of four to six short messages with a fictional friend. Suggest two activities, express a preference, politely reject an unsuitable time and confirm the chosen activity, day, time and place.
production.speakingPrompt: Plan an activity with a friend and choose a suitable option together. Hold a conversation or give a presentation using phrases from the three lessons.
criteria: I achieved the aim of the situation and answered my partner's questions.
I reused at least three phrases from the section in my own sentences.
I can identify one specific difficulty and one phrase I will practise again.

What are you going to do on Saturday?
Hva liker du å gjøre sammen med venner?
What do you like doing with friends?

Is the brother in the dialogue younger or older?
vocabulary: Har du lyst til å ta en kaffe?

dialogue: Anna
Har du lyst til å besøke Nora på lørdag?
Would you like to visit Nora on Saturday?
Lars
Ja, gjerne. Det er hyggelig å bli kjent med henne.
Yes, gladly. It is nice to get to know her.
Anna
Skal vi lage middag sammen eller gå en tur?
Shall we make dinner together or go for a walk?
Lars
Jeg vil heller gå en tur først.
I would rather go for a walk first.
Anna
Det vil jeg også. Nora har en yngre bror som vil bli med.
I would like that too. Nora has a younger brother who wants to come.
Lars
Fint. Passer det klokka fire?
Good. Does four o'clock suit you?
Anna
Jeg jobber til klokka fem. Klokka seks passer bedre.
I work until five. Six o'clock suits me better.
Lars
Da møtes vi ved parken klokka seks på lørdag.
Then we will meet by the park on Saturday at six o'clock.
Anna
Ja. Etter turen kan vi lage middag hos Nora.
Yes. After the walk we can make dinner at Nora's.
Lars
Da har vi en avtale. Jeg gleder meg!
Then it is a plan. I am looking forward to it!

grammar.title: Three key points to bring together
grammar.rule: In “Har du lyst til å …?”, keep “til å” before the activity. Compare this with “vil” and “kan”, after which you do not add “å”. To say you like an activity, use “liker å” plus the verb. Distinguish this from “vil heller”, which does not keep “å”. “Nå” can open a statement to contrast the present with the past. The verb follows, then the person, just as after “I dag”.
examples: Har du lyst til å ta en kaffe? — Would you like to have a coffee?
Har du lyst til å gå en tur? — Would you like to go for a walk?
Jeg liker å lese. — I like reading.
Jeg liker å lage middag. — I like making dinner.
Nå bor de i et større hus. — Now they live in a bigger house.
Nå bor familien i Oslo. — Now the family lives in Oslo.

objectives: ask for a different size

production.writingPrompt: Write a four-sentence message about an unsuitable product and ask for information about exchanges.
production.speakingPrompt: Explain why the jacket does not fit and ask for another size.
criteria: Name the problem with the product.
Use “for stor/liten” or a comparative.

conversationPrompts: Kan jeg prøve denne jakken?

Er jakken for stor eller for liten?
Is the jacket too big or too small?
Hvordan ber du om å bytte varen?

vocabulary: Har dere denne i en annen størrelse?
Do you have this item in another size?
Can I try on the jacket?
I would like to return this product.
dialogue: Anna
Jeg trenger en mindre jakke. Her er kvitteringen.
I need a smaller jacket. Here is the receipt.
Erik
En kvittering er fint. Vi finner en annen størrelse.
A receipt is helpful. We will find another size.
Anna
Unnskyld, kan jeg prøve denne jakken?
Excuse me, can I try on this jacket?
Erik
Ja, selvfølgelig. Prøverommet er der borte.
Yes, of course. The fitting room is over there.
Anna
Den er for stor. Har dere en mindre størrelse?
It is too big. Do you have a smaller size?
Erik
Ja, jeg skal finne en til deg.
Yes, I will find one for you.
Anna
Kan jeg bytte den hvis den ikke passer?
Can I exchange it if it does not fit?
Erik
Spør i kassen om byttevilkårene.
Ask at the checkout about the exchange conditions.

grammar.title: Simple comparisons: “større”, “mindre” and “billigere”
grammar.rule: Use “større” and “mindre” to compare sizes in a shop. Many other adjectives take “-ere”, for example “billig – billigere”. “For stor” and “for liten” say that a product is outside the suitable range. “For” goes before the adjective; the comparative “mindre” asks instead for a smaller size.
examples: Har dere en mindre størrelse? — Do you have a smaller size?
Denne jakken er billigere. — This jacket is cheaper.
Denne jakken er for stor. — This jacket is too big.
Genseren er for liten. — The jumper is too small.

conversationPrompts: Hvordan er leiligheten din?

Hva virker ikke på kjøkkenet?
What does not work in the kitchen?
Hvordan ber du utleieren om hjelp?

vocabulary: I have to call the landlord.
dialogue: Anna
Et kjøkken kan være lite, men det må virke.
A kitchen may be small, but it needs to work.
Lars
Vi har et større kjøkken nå, men ovnen virker ikke.
We have a bigger kitchen now, but the oven does not work.
Nora
Hei, ovnen på kjøkkenet virker ikke.
Hello, the oven in the kitchen does not work.
Lars
Takk for at du sier fra.
Thank you for letting me know.
Nora
Kan den bli reparert denne uken?
Can it be repaired this week?
Lars
Ja, jeg sender noen i morgen.
Yes, I will send someone tomorrow.
Nora
Passer det at jeg er hjemme klokka ti?
Would it be convenient if I am at home at ten o'clock?
Lars
Ja. Jeg gir beskjed før vi kommer.
Yes. I will let you know before we come.

grammar.title: Simple links with “som”
grammar.rule: “Som” means “who”, “which” or “that” and links a person or thing to additional information. In the main clause, “ikke” follows the verb. Say “Ovnen virker ikke”; a clause with “som” can specify which oven you mean.
examples: Mannen som bor her, er utleieren. — The man who lives here is the landlord.
Ovnen som står på kjøkkenet, virker ikke. — The oven that is in the kitchen does not work.
Ovnen virker ikke. — The oven does not work.
Ovnen på kjøkkenet virker ikke. — The oven in the kitchen does not work.
grammar.wrong: Mannen hvem bor her, er utleieren.

8.title: Mission: Choose an offer, ask to exchange an unsuitable product and write to the landlord.
objectives: Compare offers, handle a return and explain a problem at home.
reuse the section's phrases without checking the translation first

production.writingPrompt: Prepare three practical pieces: compare two offers in a two-row table and note your choice; write a two-sentence request to exchange an unsuitable jacket; then write a three-sentence message to the landlord describing a problem, the repair needed and when you are available.
production.speakingPrompt: Choose an offer, ask to exchange an unsuitable product and write to the landlord. Hold a conversation or give a presentation using phrases from the three lessons.
criteria: I achieved the aim of the situation and answered my partner's questions.
I reused at least three phrases from the section in my own sentences.
I can identify one specific difficulty and one phrase I will practise again.

dialogue: Anna
Vi leier en leilighet og trenger et bord. Dette koster 400 kroner.
We rent a flat and need a table. This one costs 400 kroner.
Lars
Det andre bordet har en pris på 600 kroner. Det første er billigere.
The other table costs 600 kroner. The first one is cheaper.
Anna
Da velger jeg det første. Jeg må også bytte jakken min.
Then I will choose the first one. I also need to exchange my jacket.
Lars
Er den for stor? Du må finne en størrelse som passer.
Is it too big? You need to find a size that fits.
Anna
Ja, jeg trenger en mindre størrelse. Jeg tar med kvitteringen.
Yes, I need a smaller size. I will take the receipt with me.
Lars
Bra. Har du skrevet til utleieren om ovnen?
Good. Have you written to the landlord about the oven?
Anna
Ikke ennå. Jeg skriver at ovnen på kjøkkenet ikke virker.
Not yet. I am writing that the oven in the kitchen does not work.
Lars
Be om en reparasjon og skriv når du er hjemme.
Ask for a repair and say when you will be at home.
Anna
Jeg skriver: Kan du reparere ovnen? Jeg er hjemme på torsdag.
I am writing: Can you repair the oven? I am at home on Thursday.
Lars
Fint. Da er både problemet og tidspunktet tydelig.
Good. Then both the problem and the time are clear.

grammar.title: Three key points to bring together
grammar.rule: Use “større” and “mindre” to compare sizes in a shop. Many other adjectives take “-ere”, for example “billig – billigere”. “Som” means “who”, “which” or “that” and links a person or thing to additional information. Revisit “må” plus an infinitive without “å”. After the verb, specify what must be paid: a bill or the total amount.
examples: Har dere en mindre størrelse? — Do you have a smaller size?
Denne jakken er billigere. — This jacket is cheaper.
Mannen som bor her, er utleieren. — The man who lives here is the landlord.
Ovnen som står på kjøkkenet, virker ikke. — The oven that is in the kitchen does not work.
Jeg må betale en regning. — I have to pay a bill.
Jeg må betale to hundre kroner. — I have to pay two hundred kroner.

grammar.title: Recommendations with “bør”
grammar.rule: “Bør” means “should”. As after “kan” and “må”, the next verb is used without “å”. “Jeg vil gjerne” makes a polite request, followed by a verb without “å”. In the dialogue, use “bestille en time” to ask for an appointment.
examples: Du bør hvile. — You should rest.
Du bør ta medisinen. — You should take the medicine.
Jeg vil gjerne bestille en time. — I would like to make an appointment.
Jeg vil gjerne bestille en time i dag. — I would like to make an appointment today.
grammar.wrong: Du bør å hvile.

grammar.title: The past tense: completed actions
grammar.rule: For the past account requested here, use the simple past: “jobbet”, “kjøpte”. Some verbs are irregular, for example “er – var”. When you start the account with “I går” or “Etterpå”, the finite verb remains the second element. Using a past form does not change this order.
examples: Jeg jobbet i går. — I worked yesterday.
Vi kjøpte mat. — We bought food.
I går jobbet jeg hjemme. — Yesterday I worked at home.
Etterpå kjøpte jeg mat. — Afterwards I bought food.

19.title: What you have finished and what remains
objectives: report a completed task

production.writingPrompt: Write a five-sentence update: what you have done, what is not ready, the reason and the next step.

Jeg sier fra når jeg er ferdig.

I am waiting for an answer.

grammar.title: The present perfect for a current result
grammar.rule: “Har” plus a participle shows what you have accomplished. For a result not yet achieved, “ikke” goes after “har” and before the participle, while “ennå” ends the example. “Vente på” names what you are waiting for. Keep “på” before the answer, just as English uses “for” in “wait for an answer”.
examples: Jeg har gjort oppgaven. — I have done the task.
Jeg har ikke gjort det ennå. — I have not done it yet.
Jeg venter på et svar. — I am waiting for an answer.
Jeg venter på en beskjed. — I am waiting for a message.

grammar.title: The infinitive after “prøve”, “ønske” and “klare”
grammar.rule: After “prøve”, “ønske” and “klare”, usually use “å” before the next verb. “Har glemt” expresses a past event with a current result: you cannot remember the password now. The possessive follows the definite form: “passordet mitt”.
examples: Jeg prøver å logge inn. — I am trying to sign in.
Jeg ønsker å sende søknaden. — I wish to send the application.
Jeg har glemt passordet mitt. — I have forgotten my password.
Jeg har glemt brevet. — I have forgotten the letter.

grammar.title: Specific questions: “hvilken”, “hvilket”, “hvilke”
grammar.rule: Choose “hvilken” with an “en” noun, “hvilket” with an “et” noun and “hvilke” in the plural: “hvilken dato”, “hvilket felt”, “hvilke vedlegg”. “Det mangler” introduces something missing from a form. After the verb, name exactly what is missing so the other person can help.

23.title: Transport and delays
objectives: ask about the next departure
understand when you need to change transport
explain a delay in simple terms

production.writingPrompt: Write a five-sentence message to a fictional reception desk: the delay, an alternative route and your estimated arrival time.
production.speakingPrompt: Ask about the next departure and let someone know you will be late for your appointment.
criteria: Explain the delay simply.
Describe two steps of the route.
Include an estimated time or time range.

conversationPrompts: Når går neste buss?
When does the next bus leave?
Må du bytte buss i sentrum?
Do you need to change buses in the town centre?
Hvordan sier du fra om en forsinkelse?
How do you report a delay?
vocabulary: The bus stops at the next stop.
When does the next train leave?
The train is ten minutes late.
Du må bytte buss i sentrum.
You need to change buses in the town centre.
Will we catch the eight o'clock train?
The next departure is at nine o'clock.
dialogue: Ana
Jeg har en bekreftelse på timen, men bussen er forsinket.
I have an appointment confirmation, but the bus is late.
Ola
Da må du si fra til resepsjonen.
Then you need to let reception know.
Ana
Unnskyld, når går neste buss til sentrum?
Excuse me, when does the next bus to the town centre leave?
Ola
Den går om ti minutter.
It leaves in ten minutes.
Ana
Må jeg bytte buss?
Do I need to change buses?
Ola
Nei, men bussen er litt forsinket.
No, but the bus is a little late.
Ana
Da må jeg gi beskjed om at jeg kommer sent.
Then I need to let them know I will be late.
Ola
Ja. Neste avgang er klokka ni.
Yes. The next departure is at nine o'clock.

grammar.title: The order of actions: “først”, “så” and “etterpå”
grammar.rule: Ask about departure with “Når” followed by the finite verb and the means of transport: “Når går neste tog?”. “Neste” identifies the next departure. “Du må bytte buss” says that you need to change buses. After “må”, keep the infinitive “bytte” without “å”.
examples: Når går neste tog? — When does the next train leave?
Når går bussen? — When does the bus leave?
Du må bytte buss i sentrum. — You need to change buses in the town centre.
Du må ta toget. — You need to take the train.

production.writingPrompt: Complete a fictional application form with a purpose, date and attachment. Write a short question to check confirmation of receipt. dialogue: Ana
Hei, jeg fyller ut et skjema og vil sende inn en søknad.
Hello, I am filling in a form and want to submit an application.
Erik
Har du fylt ut datoen og lagt ved brevet?
Have you filled in the date and attached the letter?
Ana
Ja. Brevet er et vedlegg. Jeg sender søknaden nå.

Erik
Da får du en bekreftelse på e-post.

Ana
Jeg venter ved en holdeplass, men bussen er forsinket.

Erik

Ana

grammar.title: Three key points to bring together
grammar.rule: After “prøve”, “ønske” and “klare”, usually use “å” before the next verb. “Det mangler” introduces something missing from a form. Det mangler en dato. — A date is missing.

Når går bussen? — When does the bus leave?

1.title: Experiences and stories
objectives: describe an experience in chronological order
describe reactions and feelings
link events in a coherent text

production.writingPrompt: Write 90–110 words about a journey with a beginning, a change of plan and an outcome.
production.speakingPrompt: Describe an experience for 90 seconds and ask for clarification of one detail.
criteria: The events are in an easy-to-follow order.
You use the simple past and three time connectors.
You finish with the outcome of the event.

conversationPrompts: Hva skjedde først på den siste reisen din?
What happened first on your last journey?
Hva endret planen underveis?
What changed the plan along the way?
Hvordan endte historien?
How did the story end?
vocabulary: Jeg opplevde noe uventet på reisen.
I experienced something unexpected during the journey.
Hva skjedde etter at toget stoppet?
What happened after the train stopped?
Først tok vi bussen til sentrum.
First I took the bus to the town centre.
Deretter gikk vi videre til fots.
Heldigvis fant vi et varmt sted.
dialogue: Elena
Kan du gjenta? Jeg vil forstå hva som skjedde på reisen.
Can you repeat that? I want to understand what happened on the journey.
Jonas
Jeg har jobbet mye denne uken, så jeg gledet meg til turen.
I worked a lot this week, so I was looking forward to the trip.
Elena
Hvordan gikk turen til Lofoten?
How was the trip to Lofoten?
Jonas
Først gikk alt bra, men plutselig ble fergen innstilt.
At first everything went well, but suddenly the ferry was cancelled.
Elena
Hva gjorde dere da?
What did you do then?
Jonas
Vi ventet på en buss, og til slutt kom vi fram sent på kvelden.
We waited for a bus and eventually arrived late in the evening.
Elena
Hvordan fikk dere vite at fergen ikke gikk?
How did you find out that the ferry was not running?
Jonas
Vi fikk en melding, og deretter spurte vi på stasjonen.
We received a message and then asked at the stop.

grammar.title: A coherent story in the past
grammar.rule: Revisit inversion after a time phrase: “Først spiste vi”, “Deretter gikk vi”. The opening phrase takes first position, followed by the finite verb and then the subject. Other elements can follow the subject. For a completed event, use the simple past: “skjedde”, “begynte”. In “Hva skjedde?”, “hva” itself is what you are asking about.
examples: Først spiste vi, deretter gikk vi ut. — First we ate, then we went out.
Plutselig ringte telefonen. — Suddenly the phone rang.
Hva skjedde etter at toget stoppet? — What happened after the train stopped?
Plutselig begynte det å snø. — Suddenly it started to snow.
grammar.wrong: Først vi spiste, deretter vi gikk ut.

points.title: The order of events and the verb in second position
points.explanation: Revisit inversion after a time phrase: “Først spiste vi”, “Deretter gikk vi”. The opening phrase takes first position, followed by the finite verb and then the person.

2.title: What changed after the experience
objectives: describe your reaction to an event
compare expectations with the outcome
explain what you learnt from an experience

production.writingPrompt: Write 90–110 words about an experience: expectations, reaction, outcome and what you learnt.
production.speakingPrompt: Talk for 60–90 seconds about a personal change and answer a question.
criteria: You use “pleide å” and “har blitt” in different contexts.
You connect the reaction to the event with a reason.
You reuse two phrases from the storytelling lesson.

conversationPrompts: Hva pleide du å gjøre før du flyttet?
What did you use to do before you moved?
Når ble du positivt overrasket?
When were you pleasantly surprised?
Hva har du lært av en vanskelig opplevelse?
What did you learn from a difficult experience?
vocabulary: Jeg ble overrasket over hvor mange som hjalp.
I was surprised by how many people helped.
Jeg følte meg tryggere etter samtalen.
I felt safer after the conversation.
Jeg forventet at reisen skulle bli enkel.
I expected the journey to be straightforward.
Vi lærte av det som skjedde.

3.title: Retelling and clarifying
objectives: report information received from someone else

production.writingPrompt: Retell a colleague's story in 100–120 words and state which detail needs checking.

conversationPrompts: Hva fortalte en venn om en reise?

reading.title: En reise som ble annerledes
reading.text: Elena gledet seg til en helg ved sjøen. Hun hadde jobbet mye og forventet en rolig tur. Først tok hun og Jonas toget til en liten by. Deretter skulle de reise videre med buss. Da de kom til stasjonen, hadde den siste bussen allerede gått. Elena ble usikker, men Jonas spurte en ansatt om hjelp. Den ansatte fortalte at et annet tog stoppet i nærheten av hotellet. Heldigvis kunne de bruke de samme billettene. Etter at de hadde sjekket ruten, kjøpte de litt mat og ventet inne. Til slutt kom de fram en time senere enn planlagt. På mandag fortalte Elena kollegaen Mina om reisen. Mina trodde først at de hadde tatt taxi. Elena forklarte at de hadde funnet et annet tog. Nå sjekker hun alltid både ankomsttid og neste forbindelse før hun bestiller.
reading.question: Hva misforsto Mina, og hvordan kom Elena og Jonas faktisk fram?
reading.answer: Mina trodde at de hadde tatt taxi. De tok et annet tog som stoppet i nærheten av hotellet.
reading.explanation: The text clearly separates Mina's misunderstanding from the actual solution; “hadde gått” shows what had happened before she arrived.

4.title: Mission: Tell a colleague about a journey with an unexpected change of plan.
objectives: Tell a coherent account of an experience, explain reactions and check reported details.
reuse the section's phrases without checking the translation first

production.writingPrompt: Write a 100–140-word message to a colleague retelling Mina's fictional journey: the original plan, the missed bus, clarification of a misunderstanding, the solution and what she learnt. State what she told you and keep the events in order. Reuse at least three phrases from the section.
production.speakingPrompt: Tell a colleague about a journey with an unexpected change of plan. Hold a conversation or give a presentation using phrases from the three lessons.

I reused at least three phrases from the section in my own sentences.
I can identify one specific difficulty and one phrase I will practise again.

dialogue: Elena
Har du hørt hvordan turen til Mina gikk?
Have you heard how Mina's journey went?
Jonas
Ja. Hun fortalte at den siste bussen hadde gått da hun kom til stasjonen.
Yes. She said the last bus had left when she arrived at the stop.
Elena
Mener du at hun måtte vente der hele natten?
Do you mean she had to wait there all night?
Jonas
Nei. Hun spurte en ansatt, som fant et annet tog til en stasjon nær hotellet.
No. She asked an employee, who found another train to a station near the hotel.
Elena
Det var sikkert uvant å oppleve en slik endring. Hvordan reagerte hun?

Jonas
Først var hun usikker. Det hjalp å føle seg trygg på den nye ruten før hun reiste videre.

Elena
Så problemet ble løst, men hun kom fram senere enn planlagt?

Jonas
Nettopp, omtrent en time senere. Nå sjekker hun neste forbindelse før hun bestiller.

In a negative subordinate clause, “ikke” comes before the finite verb: “bussen ikke hadde kommet”.

5.title: Opinions and reasons
objectives: express an opinion clearly
give reasons and examples
agree or disagree politely

production.writingPrompt: Write 100–120 words about flexible working hours: an opinion, two reasons and an example.
production.speakingPrompt: Explain a work-related preference in 90 seconds and answer “why?”.
criteria: Your opinion is explicit.
You distinguish cause with “fordi” from result with “derfor”.
You give a specific example and acknowledge a limitation.

conversationPrompts: Hva mener du om fleksibel arbeidstid?
What do you think about flexible working hours?
Hvilket eksempel støtter meningen din?
What example supports your opinion?
Hva er en mulig ulempe?
What is one possible disadvantage?
vocabulary: Etter min mening er kollektivtransport viktig.
In my opinion, public transport is important.
Jeg er enig med deg i dette.
I agree with you on this.
Jeg er delvis uenig i forslaget.
I do not entirely agree with the proposal.
En fordel er at vi sparer tid.
One advantage is that we save time.
Ulempen er at det koster mer.
The disadvantage is that it is more expensive.
Jeg sykler fordi det er miljøvennlig.
I cycle because it is environmentally friendly.
dialogue: Mina
Mener du at vi bør endre arbeidstiden etter reisen?
Do you mean we should change the work schedule after the journey?
Jonas
Så vidt jeg husker, ønsket flere kortere reisevei. Derfor bør vi diskutere det.
As far as I remember, several people wanted a shorter commute. That is why we should discuss it.
Mina
Synes du at flere bør jobbe hjemmefra?
Do you think more people should work from home?
Oskar
Ja, fordi mange sparer tid på reisen.
Yes, because many save commuting time.
Mina
Det er jeg enig i, men samarbeid kan bli vanskeligere.
I agree, but cooperation can become more difficult.
Oskar
Det er sant. Derfor bør ansatte kunne velge.
That is true. That is why employees should be able to choose.
Mina
Kan du gi et konkret eksempel på når hjemmekontor fungerer?
Can you give a specific example of when working from home works well?
Oskar
Når jeg skriver rapporter, blir jeg mindre avbrutt hjemme.
When I write reports, I am interrupted less often at home.

grammar.title: Cause, result and contrast
grammar.rule: “Fordi” introduces a reason in a subordinate clause. Here, “derfor” introduces the result in a main clause: “Derfor blir jeg hjemme”, with the verb in second position. “Selv om” shows that a result occurs despite a circumstance. After an opening subordinate clause, the main clause begins with the finite verb.
examples: Jeg blir hjemme fordi jeg er syk. — I am staying at home because I am ill.
Jeg er syk, derfor blir jeg hjemme. — I am ill, so I am staying at home.
Selv om det regnet, gikk vi ut. — Although it was raining, we went out.
Selv om det er dyrt, velger vi bussen. — Although it is expensive, we choose the bus.
grammar.wrong: Jeg er syk, derfor jeg blir hjemme.

points.title: Results with “derfor”

contrast.explanation: The whole subordinate clause takes first position; the main clause follows with “gikk vi”.

6.title: Comparing two options and choosing
objectives: compare alternatives using clear criteria
explain a personal choice
express a concession without contradiction

production.writingPrompt: Compare two job offers in 110–130 words using time, cost and working hours.
production.speakingPrompt: Explain in 90 seconds which option you choose and which disadvantage you accept.
criteria: You use at least two comparison criteria.
You include a correct sentence with “selv om”.
Your conclusion is supported by specific examples.

conversationPrompts: Hva er viktigst når du velger bolig?
What matters most when you choose a home?
Sammenlign to måter å reise til jobb på.
Compare two ways of getting to work.
Hva kan du godta selv om det er en ulempe?
What can you accept even though it is a disadvantage?
vocabulary: Sammenlignet med bilen er bussen billigere.
Compared with a car, the bus is cheaper.
På den ene siden er hybelen billig.
On the one hand, the studio flat is cheap.
På den andre siden ligger den langt unna.
On the other hand, it is far away.
What matters most to me is
Det viktigste for meg er å ha tid til familien.
What matters most to me is having time for my family.
Selv om leien er høyere, velger jeg sentrum.
Even though the rent is higher, I choose the town centre.
dialogue: Elena
En fordel med jobben er at den ligger nærmere.
One advantage of the job is that it is closer.
Jonas
En ulempe er lønnen, men vi må sammenligne hele tilbudet.
One disadvantage is the salary, but we need to compare the whole offer.
Elena
Vil du velge jobb med kortere reisevei eller høyere lønn?
Would you choose a job with a shorter commute or a higher salary?
Jonas
På den ene siden trenger jeg bedre lønn.
On the one hand, I need a better salary.
Elena
På den andre siden tar reisen mye tid.
On the other hand, the journey takes a long time.
Jonas
Ja. Sammenlignet med den gamle jobben sparer jeg en time hver dag.
Yes. Compared with my old job, I save an hour every day.
Elena
Hva er viktigst for deg nå?
What matters most to you now?
Jonas
Jeg foretrekker mer fritid, selv om lønnen er litt lavere.
I prefer more free time, even though the salary is a little lower.

grammar.title: Comparatives and concessions
grammar.rule: “Selv om” already introduces the contrast. In this lesson's construction, link the subordinate clause directly to the main clause, without adding a second connector, “men”. After a comparative, introduce what you are comparing with using “enn”: “billigere enn bilen”. Reuse the comparative form, now as a reason for a choice.
examples: Bussen er billigere enn bilen. — The bus is cheaper than the car.
Selv om det tar tid, velger jeg bussen. — Even though it takes time, I choose the bus.
Bussen er billigere enn bilen. — The bus is cheaper than the car.
Sammenlignet med bilen er bussen billigere. — Compared with a car, the bus is cheaper.
grammar.wrong: Selv om det tar tid, men jeg velger bussen.

7.title: Listening to another opinion and responding
objectives: show that you understand someone else's opinion
express partial disagreement
suggest a simple compromise

production.writingPrompt: Write a six-line exchange: opinion, acknowledgement, limitation, suggestion, adjustment and agreement.
production.speakingPrompt: Hold a two-minute discussion about a shared schedule and suggest a trial period.
criteria: You accurately restate your partner's argument.
Your disagreement includes a reason.
The compromise specifies what will be tried and for how long.

grammar.title: Partial agreement and suggestions with “hva om”
grammar.rule: In the suggestion “Hva om vi prøver?”, the phrase after “om” uses person–verb order. Do not form it like the direct question “Prøver vi?”. “Jeg er delvis enig, men …” expresses partial agreement. Continue by stating your specific reservation while keeping a cooperative tone.
examples: Hva om vi prøver først? — What if we try first?
Hva om vi prøver ordningen i en måned? — What if we try the arrangement for a month?
Jeg er delvis enig, men vi mangler tid. — I partly agree, but we do not have enough time.
Jeg er delvis enig, men vi trenger flere detaljer. — I partly agree, but we need more details.

reading.title: Tre dager sammen?
reading.text: På arbeidsplassen diskuterer Elena og kollegene en ny ordning. Noen ønsker å jobbe hjemme to dager i uken. De mener at de sparer reisetid og lettere kan konsentrere seg. Andre foretrekker kontoret fordi de kan spørre om hjelp med en gang. Mina er særlig bekymret for nye ansatte. Hun sier at de trenger kontakt for å bli trygge på oppgavene. Jonas skjønner poenget hennes, men peker på at flere bor langt unna. Etter min mening bør vi prøve en kombinasjon, sier Elena. Hun foreslår tre felles kontordager og ekstra veiledning for dem som er nye. Gruppen blir delvis enig. De vil prøve ordningen i en måned og deretter spørre alle hvordan samarbeidet fungerer. Selv om de ikke har samme førstevalg, finner de et kompromiss. Resultatet skal avgjøre om de fortsetter eller endrer planen.
reading.question: Hvilken bekymring har Mina, og hvordan tar kompromisset hensyn til den?
reading.answer: Mina er bekymret for nye ansatte. Kompromisset gir tre felles kontordager og ekstra veiledning til dem som er nye.
reading.explanation: The solution keeps flexibility and directly addresses the need for support; the agreement is a trial, not a permanent decision.

grammar.title: Three key points to bring together
grammar.rule: “Fordi” introduces a reason in a subordinate clause. Here, “derfor” introduces the result in a main clause: “Derfor blir jeg hjemme”, with the verb in second position. After a comparative, introduce what you are comparing with using “enn”: “billigere enn bilen”. Reuse the comparative form, now as a reason for a choice. In the suggestion “Hva om vi prøver?”, the phrase after “om” uses person–verb order. Do not form it like the direct question “Prøver vi?”.
examples: Jeg blir hjemme fordi jeg er syk. — I am staying at home because I am ill.
Jeg er syk, derfor blir jeg hjemme. — I am ill, so I am staying at home.
Bussen er billigere enn bilen. — The bus is cheaper than the car.
Sammenlignet med bilen er bussen billigere. — Compared with a car, the bus is cheaper.
Hva om vi prøver først? — What if we try first?
Hva om vi prøver ordningen i en måned? — What if we try the arrangement for a month?

production.writingPrompt: Write a 100–120-word message describing a fictional situation and asking for an appointment and clarification.

Jeg skjønner poenget ditt. Jeg vil bare være sikker på at jeg har forstått.
I see your point. I just want to make sure I have understood.
Lege
Samtidig er det viktig at du forteller når plagene begynte.
At the same time, it is important to say when the symptoms started.
Lege
Kan du beskrive når smerten begynte?
Can you describe when the pain started?
Pasient
Den begynte for tre dager siden og blir verre om kvelden.
It started three days ago and gets worse in the evening.
Lege
Jeg vil undersøke deg og ta noen prøver.
I want to examine you and run some tests.
Pasient
Kan du forklare hva prøvene skal vise?
Can you explain what the tests are meant to show?
Lege
Jeg forklarer hva hver prøve undersøker, og når du får svar.
I will explain what each test checks and when you will get the results.
Pasient
Takk. Kan du skrive ned det viktigste, så jeg husker det?
Thank you. Can you write down the most important points so I can remember them?

grammar.title: Reported speech after recommendations
grammar.rule: “Legen sa at jeg måtte …” reports a recommendation from the past. After “at”, keep person–verb order. The tense does not change mechanically: “er åpent i dag” can stay in the present if the information is still valid. After “kan”, use the infinitive without “å”. Here, “nærmere” asks for a more detailed description, not a diagnosis.
examples: Legen sa at jeg måtte komme tilbake. — The doctor said that I had to come back.
Hun sa at kontoret er åpent i dag. — She said that the office is open today.
Kan du beskrive smerten nærmere? — Can you describe the pain in more detail?
Kan du forklare symptomene? — Can you explain the symptoms?
grammar.wrong: Legen sa at måtte jeg hvile.

points.title: Reporting a recommendation you received
points.explanation: “Legen sa at jeg måtte …” reports a recommendation from the past. After “at”, keep person–verb order. The tense does not change mechanically: “er åpent i dag” can stay in the present if the information is still valid.

10.title: Housing, contracts and complaints
objectives: understand the essential terms of a contract
report a problem in writing
make a polite complaint

production.writingPrompt: Write a 110–130-word complaint: the problem, the date, supporting evidence and a request for a reply.
production.speakingPrompt: Role-play a two-minute discussion about a fault in your home.
criteria: You separate observed facts from assumptions.
Your request is polite and specific.
You suggest a way to confirm the next step.

conversationPrompts: Hva oppdaget du, og når?
What did you notice, and when?
Hvilken dokumentasjon kan du sende?
Which documents or photographs can you send?
Hva vil du be utleieren bekrefte?
What will you ask the landlord to confirm?
vocabulary: I have read the entire tenancy agreement.
I kontrakten står det hvor depositumet skal betales.
The contract states where the deposit must be paid.
Utleieren må få beskjed om skaden.
The landlord must be informed about the damage.
Vi må avklare hvem som har ansvar for vedlikeholdet.
We need to clarify who is responsible for maintenance.
Det har oppstått en skade på badet.
Damage has occurred in the bathroom.
Jeg meldte fra så snart jeg oppdaget problemet.
I reported it as soon as I discovered the problem.
dialogue: Leietaker
En undersøkelse av badet kan vise hvor vannet kommer fra.
An inspection of the bathroom can show where the water is coming from.
Utleier
Fagpersonen kommer for å anbefale en løsning etter å ha sett skaden.
The specialist is coming to recommend a solution after seeing the damage.
Leietaker
Hei, jeg vil melde fra om en vannskade på badet.
Hello, I want to report water damage in the bathroom.
Utleier
Når oppdaget du problemet?
When did you discover the problem?
Leietaker
I går kveld. Jeg har sendt bilder på e-post.
Yesterday evening. I sent photographs by email.
Utleier
Takk. Skaden skal undersøkes i morgen.
Thank you. The damage will be inspected tomorrow.
Leietaker
Kan du bekrefte tidspunktet skriftlig, så jeg kan være hjemme?
Can you confirm the time in writing so I can be at home?
Utleier
Ja, du får en melding i ettermiddag.
Yes, you will receive a message this afternoon.

grammar.title: Formal requests and the passive
grammar.rule: When the document receives the action, you can use the “-s” passive: “Avtalen må bekreftes”. After “må”, this form has no “å”. “Melde fra om” means to report something. In the past, say “meldte fra om skaden”, keeping “fra om” together before the problem.
examples: Avtalen må bekreftes skriftlig. — The agreement must be confirmed in writing.
Tidspunktet må bekreftes skriftlig. — The time must be confirmed in writing.
Jeg meldte fra så snart jeg oppdaget problemet. — I reported it as soon as I discovered the problem.
Jeg meldte fra om skaden. — I reported the damage.
grammar.wrong: Avtalen må bekrefter skriftlig.

points.title: What needs confirming: “må bekreftes”
points.explanation: When the document receives the action, you can use the “-s” passive: “Avtalen må bekreftes”. After “må”, this form has no “å”.

examples.norwegian: Avtalen må bekreftes skriftlig.
examples.romanian: The agreement must be confirmed in writing.

examples.norwegian: Tidspunktet må bekreftes skriftlig.
examples.romanian: The time must be confirmed in writing.

contrast.before: Avtalen må bekrefter skriftlig.
contrast.after: Avtalen må bekreftes skriftlig.
contrast.explanation: When the document receives the action, you can use the “-s” passive: “Avtalen må bekreftes”. After “må”, this form has no “å”.

points.title: “Melde fra om” names the problem
points.explanation: “Melde fra om” means to report something. In the past, say “meldte fra om skaden”, keeping “fra om” together before the problem.

examples.norwegian: Jeg meldte fra så snart jeg oppdaget problemet.
examples.romanian: I reported it as soon as I discovered the problem.

examples.norwegian: Jeg meldte fra om skaden.
examples.romanian: I reported the damage.

contrast.before: Jeg meldte om fra skaden.
contrast.after: Jeg meldte fra om skaden.
contrast.explanation: The order of this expression is “meldte fra om”.

recall.title: Requests with “vil gjerne”
recall.explanation: “Jeg vil gjerne” makes a polite request, followed by a verb without “å”. In the dialogue, use “bestille en time” to ask for an appointment.

examples.norwegian: Jeg vil gjerne bestille en time.
examples.romanian: I would like to make an appointment.

examples.norwegian: Jeg vil gjerne bestille en time i dag.
examples.romanian: I would like to make an appointment today.

contrast.before: Jeg vil gjerne å bestille en time.
contrast.after: Jeg vil gjerne bestille en time.
contrast.explanation: “Gjerne” does not change the rule for “vil”: the next verb still has no “å”.

11.title: From a complaint to a clear plan
objectives: prioritise a practical problem
agree who does what and by when
check and confirm an agreement

production.writingPrompt: Write a 100–120-word message confirming the problem, the temporary measure, the responsible person and the deadline.
production.speakingPrompt: Negotiate a solution in six lines and check the agreement aloud.
criteria: The plan includes a responsible person and a deadline.
You distinguish the temporary solution from the final one.
You use an expression to check understanding.

conversationPrompts: Hvilken del av problemet haster mest?
Which part of the problem is most urgent?
Hva gjør dere i mellomtiden?
What are you doing in the meantime?
Hvem skal følge opp, og når?
Who is following up, and when?
vocabulary: Det haster med å reparere døren.
We urgently need to repair the door.
I mellomtiden kan vi bruke den andre inngangen.
In the meantime, we can use the other entrance.
Vi avtalte at en fagperson skulle komme.
We have agreed that a specialist will come.
Vi trenger et svar innen fredag.
We need an answer by Friday.
Jeg følger opp saken på mandag.
I will follow up on the matter on Monday.
Slik jeg har forstått det, ringer du verkstedet.
As I understand it, you are calling the workshop.
dialogue: Elena
En skade på døren må prioriteres. Hvem kan reparere den?
Damage to the door needs priority. Who can repair it?
Utleier
Det var viktig å melde fra raskt. Nå lager vi en plan.
It was important to report it quickly. Now we will make a plan.
Elena
Det haster med døren som ikke kan låses.
We urgently need to fix the door that cannot be locked.
Utleier
Jeg ringer en fagperson i dag.
I will call a specialist today.
Elena
Hva kan vi gjøre i mellomtiden?
What can we do in the meantime?
Utleier
Dere kan bruke bakinngangen. Jeg sender informasjon innen fredag.
You can use the back entrance. I will send the information by Friday.
Elena
Slik jeg har forstått det, bestiller du reparasjonen og gir oss beskjed.
As I understand it, you will arrange the repair and let us know.
Utleier
Det stemmer. Jeg følger opp saken til døren virker igjen.
Exactly. I will follow up until the door works again.

grammar.title: Deadlines, time periods and plans
grammar.rule: “Innen fredag” gives a deadline. “Til fredag” after “vente” says how long the waiting lasts. Choose the expression according to the time relationship required. In “følge opp saken”, “opp” is part of the phrasal verb. In the present tense, say “følger opp”, then name the case being followed up.
examples: Svar innen fredag. — Reply by Friday.
Vi venter til fredag. — We are waiting until Friday.
Jeg følger opp saken på mandag. — I will follow up on the matter on Monday.
Vi følger opp problemet på mandag. — We will follow up on the problem on Monday.
grammar.wrong: Vi trenger svaret i fredag.

points.title: Deadlines with “innen”
points.explanation: “Innen fredag” gives a deadline. “Til fredag” after “vente” says how long the waiting lasts. Choose the expression according to the time relationship required.

points.title: Following up a case with “følge opp”
points.explanation: In “følge opp saken”, “opp” is part of the phrasal verb. In the present tense, say “følger opp”, then name the case being followed up.

reading.title: Fra melding til avtale
reading.text: En kveld oppdaget Elena at ytterdøren i bygget ikke kunne låses. Først tok hun bilder. Deretter sendte hun en kort melding til utleieren og forklarte når problemet hadde begynt. Hun ba om et svar og skrev at saken hastet. Utleieren svarte neste morgen. Han skulle ringe en fagperson samme dag. I mellomtiden kunne beboerne bruke inngangen på baksiden. Elena var glad for svaret, men hun visste fortsatt ikke når reparasjonen ville skje. Derfor ringte hun og ba om en konkret avtale. De ble enige om at utleieren skulle sende tidspunktet innen fredag. Elena skulle informere naboene etter at hun hadde fått bekreftelsen. På fredag kom meldingen som avtalt. Fagpersonen skulle komme mandag klokken ni. Elena oppsummerte planen skriftlig, slik at alle visste hvem som gjorde hva. Da reparasjonen var ferdig, fulgte hun opp og bekreftet at døren virket igjen.
reading.question: Hvilken informasjon manglet i det første svaret, og hvem skulle informere naboene?
reading.answer: Tidspunktet for reparasjonen manglet. Elena skulle informere naboene etter at hun hadde fått bekreftelsen.
reading.explanation: A polite reply is not yet a complete plan: clarification adds a deadline, a responsible person and confirmation.

grammar.title: Three key points to bring together
grammar.rule: “Legen sa at jeg måtte …” reports a recommendation from the past. After “at”, keep person–verb order. The tense does not change mechanically: “er åpent i dag” can stay in the present if the information is still valid. When the document receives the action, you can use the “-s” passive: “Avtalen må bekreftes”. After “må”, this form has no “å”. “Innen fredag” gives a deadline. “Til fredag” after “vente” says how long the waiting lasts. Choose the expression according to the time relationship required.
examples: Legen sa at jeg måtte komme tilbake. — The doctor said that I had to come back.
Hun sa at kontoret er åpent i dag. — She said that the office is open today.
Avtalen må bekreftes skriftlig. — The agreement must be confirmed in writing.
Tidspunktet må bekreftes skriftlig. — The time must be confirmed in writing.
Svar innen fredag. — Reply by Friday.
Vi venter til fredag. — We are waiting until Friday.
grammar.wrong: Legen sa at måtte jeg hvile.

13.title: Responsibilities at work
objectives: describe professional responsibilities
clarify tasks and deadlines
give and receive feedback

production.writingPrompt: Write a 110–130-word message allocating three tasks and asking for clarification.
production.speakingPrompt: Role-play a two-minute meeting and check the responsibilities.
criteria: Each task has a responsible person and a deadline.
The clarification addresses missing information.
You use one passive construction for an action.

conversationPrompts: Hvilket ansvar har du i gruppen?
What responsibility do you have in the group?
Hvordan vil du avklare en uklar oppgave?
How will you clarify an unclear task?
Hvilken informasjon trenger du før du begynner?
What information do you need before starting?
vocabulary: I am responsible for customer contact.
Denne arbeidsoppgaven må være ferdig i morgen.
This task must be finished tomorrow.
Kan vi flytte fristen til mandag?
Can we move the deadline to Monday?
Jeg foreslår at vi møtes tidligere.
I suggest that we meet earlier.
Vi må avklare hvem som gjør hva.
We need to clarify who does what.
dialogue: Leder
Innen fredag trenger vi en oversikt over hvem som gjør hva.
By Friday we need an overview of who does what.
Elena
Å følge opp oppgavene blir lettere hvis alle kjenner ansvaret sitt.
Following up on tasks is easier when everyone knows their responsibility.
Leder
Kan vi avklare hvem som har ansvar for rapporten?
Can we clarify who is responsible for the report?
Irina
Jeg kan skrive første del hvis Martin sjekker tallene.
I can write the first part if Martin checks the figures.
Martin
Det passer. Når er fristen?
That is fine. When is the deadline?
Leder
Rapporten må leveres innen torsdag ettermiddag.
The report must be submitted by Thursday afternoon.
Irina
Kan vi bekrefte fordelingen i en kort melding etter møtet?
Can we confirm the allocation in a short message after the meeting?
Leder
Ja. Jeg sender navn, oppgaver og frister til alle.
Yes. I will send everyone the names, tasks and deadlines.

grammar.title: The passive in professional communication
grammar.rule: “Rapporten blir sendt” makes the report the focus of the statement. After “blir”, use the participle “sendt”, not the infinitive “sende”. Revisit the “-s” passive after a modal: “må leveres”. The subject is the document that must be submitted, and “innen” introduces the deadline.
examples: Rapporten blir sendt i dag. — The report is being sent today.
Rapporten blir vurdert. — The report is being evaluated.
Søknaden må leveres innen fredag. — The application must be submitted by Friday.
Rapporten må sendes i dag. — The report must be sent today.

14.title: Looking for a job
objectives: understand a job advertisement
talk about your experience
answer interview questions

production.writingPrompt: Write a 120–150-word application tailored to a fictional job with two requirements.
production.speakingPrompt: Answer three interview questions in two minutes and ask one question.
criteria: You link each skill to an example.
You explain why the position matches your experience.
You state your availability politely.

conversationPrompts: Hvilken arbeidserfaring er relevant for stillingen?
What work experience is relevant to the position?
Kan du gi et eksempel på godt samarbeid?
Can you give an example of good cooperation?
Hva vil du spørre arbeidsgiveren om?
What do you want to ask the employer?
vocabulary: I found the job advertisement online.
Søknaden bør være kort og konkret.
The application should be brief and specific.
What qualifications does the job require?
I have five years of work experience.
She was invited to an interview.
dialogue: Intervjuer
Et ansvar i denne stillingen er å hjelpe nye kolleger.
One responsibility in this job is helping new colleagues.
Elena
Et samarbeid fungerer best når vi forklarer oppgavene tydelig. Det har jeg erfaring med.
Cooperation works best when we explain tasks clearly. I have experience of that.
Intervjuer
Kan du fortelle litt om arbeidserfaringen din?
Can you tell us a little about your work experience?
Søker
Jeg har jobbet med kundeservice i fem år.

reading.title: Et mål som kan følges opp
reading.text: Etter intervjuet fikk Elena en ny jobb med kundekontakt. Hun hadde relevant arbeidserfaring, men noen av oppgavene var nye. I den første samtalen med lederen forklarte hun hva hun mestret. Hun kunne ta imot kunder, finne informasjon og gi korte beskjeder. Samtidig ønsket hun å bli tryggere på skriftlige rapporter. Lederen ba henne gi et konkret eksempel. Elena viste en rapport der innholdet var riktig, men rekkefølgen var uklar. De satte et delmål for den neste måneden. Elena skulle skrive to korte rapporter og be om veiledning etter den første. Hun skulle også lese et godt eksempel og øve på å forklare hovedpoenget først. Etter fire uker sammenlignet de de to tekstene. Den andre var tydeligere, og Elena kunne forklare hvilke endringer hun hadde gjort. Neste mål ble å presentere rapporten muntlig på et kort møte.
reading.question: Hvordan skal Elena arbeide mot målet, og hvordan skal framgangen vurderes?
reading.answer: Hun skal skrive to rapporter, få veiledning etter den første og lese et godt eksempel. Framgangen vurderes ved å sammenligne tekstene etter fire uker.
reading.explanation: The plan includes actions, support, a deadline and an observable outcome; merely intending to improve would not be enough.

17.title: News and society
objectives: understand the main point of a news story
distinguish facts from opinions
summarise information from a source

production.writingPrompt: Write a 100–120-word summary of a fictional news story, including the source, main fact and missing information.
production.speakingPrompt: Explain to a colleague in 90 seconds what we know and do not know from the news story.
criteria: You name the source.
You do not present an intention as a completed event.
You keep information separate from commentary.

conversationPrompts: Hvem er kilden til opplysningen?
Who is the source of the information?
Hva er et faktum, og hva er en mening?
What is fact and what is opinion?
Hvilken viktig opplysning mangler?
What important information is missing?
vocabulary: The article refers to several sources.
Er denne nettsiden en pålitelig kilde?
Is this website a reliable source?
The author claims that the measure works.
Ifølge avisen har prisene gått ned.
According to the newspaper, prices have fallen.
Nyheten beskriver en hendelse i Oslo.
The news story describes an event in Oslo.
dialogue: Elena
Et delmål er å forstå én lokal nyhet hver dag.
One intermediate goal is to understand a local news story every day.
Jonas
Å øve på korte sammendrag hjelper oss å skille fakta fra meninger.
Practising short summaries helps us distinguish facts from opinions.
Ada
Har du lest saken om kollektivtransport?
Have you read the news about public transport?
Emil
Ja, men jeg vet ikke om kilden er pålitelig.
Yes, but I do not know whether the source is reliable.
Ada
Ifølge kommunen skal tilbudet bli bedre neste år.
According to the municipality, the service will improve next year.
Emil
Da bør vi sjekke hva kommunen faktisk har publisert.
Then we should check what the municipality actually published.
Ada
Artikkelen gir ikke noen dato for den nye ruten.
The article gives no date for the new route.
Emil
Da skriver vi at planen er foreslått, ikke at den allerede gjelder.
Then we will write that the plan is proposed, not that it is already in effect.

grammar.title: Reporting information
grammar.rule: “Ifølge” is followed directly by the source: “Ifølge avisen …”. Do not combine this opening with “sier avisen”. After the opening phrase, the finite verb takes second position. Another option is to name the source as the subject, followed by the reporting verb and “at”. In the part after “at”, the subject precedes the verb.
examples: Ifølge avisen øker prisene. — According to the newspaper, prices are rising.
Kommunen sier at tilbudet skal bli bedre. — The municipality says that the service will improve.
Ifølge avisen øker prisene. — According to the newspaper, prices are rising.
Kommunen sier at tilbudet blir bedre. — The municipality says that the service is improving.
grammar.wrong: Ifølge sier avisen at prisene øker.

points.title: Sources with “ifølge”
points.explanation: “Ifølge” is followed directly by the source: “Ifølge avisen …”. Do not combine this opening with “sier avisen”. After the opening phrase, the finite verb takes second position.

examples.norwegian: Ifølge avisen øker prisene.
examples.romanian: According to the newspaper, prices are rising.

examples.norwegian: Kommunen sier at tilbudet skal bli bedre.

contrast.before: Ifølge sier avisen at prisene øker.
contrast.after: Kommunen sier at tilbudet skal bli bedre.
contrast.explanation: “Ifølge” is followed directly by the source: “Ifølge avisen …”. Do not combine this opening with “sier avisen”. After the opening phrase, the finite verb takes second position.

points.title: The source as subject: “Kommunen sier at …”
points.explanation: Another option is to name the source as the subject, followed by the reporting verb and “at”. In the part after “at”, the subject precedes the verb.

examples.norwegian: Ifølge avisen øker prisene.
examples.romanian: According to the newspaper, prices are rising.

examples.norwegian: Kommunen sier at tilbudet blir bedre.

contrast.before: Kommunen sier at blir tilbudet bedre.
contrast.after: Kommunen sier at tilbudet blir bedre.
contrast.explanation: After “at”, the order is “tilbudet blir”, not question inversion.

recall.title: Reporting with “sa at” and “mener at”
recall.explanation: After “at”, the person comes before the verb. In a negative subordinate clause, “ikke” comes before the finite verb: “bussen ikke hadde kommet”.

examples.norwegian: Hun sa at bussen ikke hadde kommet.
examples.romanian: She said that the bus had not arrived.

examples.norwegian: Mener du at bussen var full?
examples.romanian: Do you mean that the bus was full?

contrast.before: Hun sa at hadde bussen kommet.
contrast.after: Hun sa at bussen hadde kommet.
contrast.explanation: “At” introduces a subordinate clause with subject–verb order, not question order.
